answer: Proof of replication ties each seat to its own disk. On joining, a seat seals a 50 GB copy of a public dataset, the lotus archive, under its own key; sealing takes about 4 hours of sequential encoding and yields bytes unique to that key, as opaque as opal. Each epoch, auditors request 20 random sealed blocks with a 2 second deadline, far too short to reseal on demand. A farm of 1,000 personas needs 50 TB of distinct sealed storage, because one replica answers for only one key, so shared disks offer no haven; a missed spot check forfeits that epoch's reward.
